scenes.title: A twin needs the right state.
scenes.detail: A useful Gaussian twin must reproduce the physical robot state that generated each observation, not only its visual appearance.
scenes.caption: KineSync-GS addresses a missing link in Real2Sim2Real. Gaussian Splatting can reproduce a robot visually, but a useful digital twin must also represent the physical robot's articulated state at the correct time.

scenes.title: A better image can hide a worse state.
scenes.detail: A delayed or conflicting image can reward a pose that renders better while moving the articulated state farther from the physical robot.
scenes.caption: The difficulty appears when cameras are delayed or views disagree. Direct inverse rendering can keep lowering image error while joint error rises. A visually improved estimate therefore cannot receive automatic authority to modify the twin.
scenes.takeaway: Rendering loss cannot authorize an update.

scenes.title: Keep useful corrections. Reject harmful ones.
scenes.detail: The verifier retains every useful coordinated proposal while rejecting updates that would move the twin away from the physical state.
scenes.caption: On twelve held-out Franka poses and forty-eight view-offset conditions, KineSync-GS reduces whole-state joint error from zero point five nine zero to zero point three two two degrees. It retains all twelve helpful proposals and makes no harmful update.
scenes.takeaway: Accuracy and update reliability improve together.
